sources.name: Unicode CLDR
sources.version: 48.0 (as shipped in ICU 78.3 with Node 22.23.4; plural rules compared with cldr-json main on 2026-11-11)

provenance.notes: Written in this phase from the cited references and re-expressed; the Arabic text is the researcher's own wording and needs a native reviewer. The checks are proposals for the harness, not yet run.

statement.ar: كل رسالة فيها عدد تُكتب بالصيغ الست التي تعرّفها CLDR للعربية (zero، one، two، few، many، other) وتُختار الصيغة بالقاعدة، لا بشرط «إذا كان العدد واحدًا».
statement.en: Every message containing a count is written in the six forms CLDR defines for Arabic (zero, one, two, few, many, other) and the form is selected by the rule, not by an "if the count is one" condition.

rationale.ar: المعدود في العربية يتغير: مفرد، مثنى، جمع للأعداد 3–10، مفرد منصوب للأعداد 11–99، مفرد مجرور للمئة والألف. «3 ملف» و«11 ملفات» خطآن يراهما كل قارئ. ومكتبات شائعة تقدم للعربية صيغتين فقط.
rationale.en: The counted noun changes in Arabic: singular, dual, plural for 3–10, accusative singular for 11–99, genitive singular for hundreds and thousands. «3 ملف» and «11 ملفات» are errors every reader sees. Common libraries ship only two forms for Arabic.

checks: plural-agreement: the selected category equals expected.category for all 102 cases.
Every Arabic plural message defines all six categories (or declares which are impossible for its range).
Component-internal strings with counts (selected items, results, pages, characters remaining) pass the same test.
For counts 0, 1 and 2 the phrase contains no digit when the form expresses the number in words.
